answer.summary: The observations DO NOT support the claim; NH3 directly refutes it. Although NH3 has three sigma bonds, its central nitrogen has one lone pair, giving steric number 4 (sp3 hybridisation, trigonal pyramidal shape). A more defensible introductory rule is: 'Central atom hybridisation is determined by total electron domains (steric number = sigma bonds + lone pairs), where steric number 3 corresponds to sp2 and steric number 4 corresponds to sp3.' Shape observations alone (measured positions of nuclei) prove molecular geometry, but do not prove that hybrid orbitals physically exist; hybridisation is a mathematical Valence Bond model constructed to rationalize observed shapes.

questions.stem: A student says, 'If the electron-domain geometry is tetrahedral, the atoms must form a tetrahedral molecular shape.' Evaluate the statement using CH4, NH3 and H2O, with their respective central lone-pair counts of zero, one and two.

difficulty.basis: Evaluating the student statement using CH4 (0 LP, tetrahedral), NH3 (1 LP, pyramidal), and H2O (2 LP, bent), proving the statement is false and providing the decisive warrant.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Four-domain geometry equals the atom-only shape in every case.

grade9v3:learning_repair.clarify: Test whether domain geometry and nuclear shape are interchangeable.
grade9v3:learning_repair.connect: A lone-pair domain has no bonded nucleus to include in molecular-shape naming.
grade9v3:learning_repair.way: Hold four domains fixed and vary how many slots are bonded atoms.
grade9v3:learning_repair.rule: CH4, NH3, H2O have four introductory domains but tetrahedral, pyramidal and bent nuclear shapes respectively.
grade9v3:learning_repair.check: Changed check: a four-bond/no-lone-pair centre cannot be assigned the same atom-only shape as a two-bond/two-lone-pair centre.
grade9v3:learning_repair.probe: For four-domain inventories with 4,3,2 bonded atoms, give the atom-only shape and explain omitted slots.
grade9v3:learning_repair.pattern: Tetrahedral, pyramidal, bent; omitted slots are lone pairs. Repeating tetrahedral for all atom-only shapes exposes the conflation.
grade9v3:learning_repair.transfer: Sketch the domain and atom-only inventories separately for H2O.

answer.summary: The student's statement is FALSE. While CH4, NH3, and H2O all have tetrahedral electron-domain geometry (steric number 4), their molecular shapes differ based on central lone pair counts: CH4 (0 lone pairs) has 4 bonded atoms -> tetrahedral molecular shape; NH3 (1 lone pair) has 3 bonded atoms -> trigonal pyramidal molecular shape; H2O (2 lone pairs) has 2 bonded atoms -> bent / angular molecular shape. Decisive warrant: Electron-domain geometry describes the arrangement of all electron pairs (bonding + non-bonding), whereas molecular shape describes exclusively the spatial arrangement of atomic nuclei. Shape matches domain geometry only when the central atom has zero lone pairs.

reasoning_route.action: Evaluate the statement as false by comparing CH4, NH3, and H2O.
reasoning_route.why_valid: NH3 and H2O serve as direct counterexamples to the claim.

reasoning_route.action: Map each molecule: CH4 is tetrahedral, NH3 is trigonal pyramidal, H2O is bent.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Positions of nuclei define molecular shape.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: State decisive warrant: electron geometry tracks all domains; shape tracks nuclei only.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Non-bonding lone pairs occupy domain vertices without creating visible atomic vertices in molecular shape.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions
